info.title: origin API
info.description: The repositories an origin server hosts: their records, targets, landing queues and events.

get.summary: The OpenAPI document of this API.
Lists the repositories on the server that the caller sees.

401.description: The token is invalid or expired

post.summary:
Lists what the repository holds of some changes: their revisions,
heads and statements, by id.

200.description: An inventory for each change, in the order asked: empty for a change the repository never heard of

get.summary: Lists the revisions of a change, and its heads.

200.description: The revisions, in the order the repository received them

404.description: The repository or the change does not exist

get.summary:
Reads the events after a cursor, waiting up to `wait` for some: a
long-poll. Pass the page's `next` as the next request's cursor.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
The cursor to read after: the `next` of the previous page. By
default, the end of the stream, so only new events come.

parameters.name: generation
parameters.description:
The generation of the op log the cursor is of, as its page said. A
cursor of another generation, such as from before the repository
was restored, has expired.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description:
How long to wait for events, such as `30s`. Without it, the answer
comes at once, possibly empty.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Stop after about this many events: an entry's events are delivered
whole.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description:
Only events of these names or statement kinds, comma-separated, such
as `check.requested,ci.*`.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description:
Only events whose subject starts with one of these, comma-separated,
such as a revision id prefix, `change:3fa2` or `main`.

200.description: The events, oldest first, and the next cursor: empty if none came in time

410.description: The server no longer keeps the events after the cursor

get.summary: Reads a file of a snapshot, as `tree` finds it.

parameters.name: at
parameters.description:
The snapshot: a target, such as `main`, or `revision:<id>` or
`acceptance:<id>`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The directory or file: the root by default.

400.description: The path is a directory, or the record has no snapshot

403.description: The caller may not read the file

404.description: The repository, the target, the record or the path does not exist

post.summary:
Submits a change, or a target's tip, to a target's landing queue, run
by this server.

200.description: How each landing went: landed, unchanged, or waiting for evidence or a conflict's resolution

400.description: A target was proposed without a target to land on

404.description: The repository, the change or a target does not exist

409.description: The change diverged or was abandoned, or this server doesn't order the target

get.summary: Lists the landings that wait, and why.
Lists the acceptances of a target, oldest first.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description:
The position of the first acceptance to return: 0, the first, by
default.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Return at most this many acceptances: all by default.

404.description: The repository or the target does not exist

post.summary:
Promotes results to a record from the records with the same input
digest, as statements this server issues, and retries the landings
waiting for them.

200.description: The statements promoted: none if nothing matched

404.description: The repository or the record does not exist

put.summary:
Puts a batch of objects, as a pack: snapshots, revisions and
statements, each needing only objects the batch or the repository has,
of the kinds it names. With `expect`, only if the changes it names have
the heads it says when the records are published.

parameters.name: expect
parameters.description:
The heads of changes as the caller saw them, comma-separated, each
`<change>=<head>+<head>`, or `<change>=` for a change the repository
didn't have. The batch is refused if one's heads differ now.

400.description: The pack is invalid, holds an acceptance, or needs objects the repository doesn't have, or has as another kind

409.description: A change of `expect` has other heads now

post.summary: Fetches records by id, each with the blob it carries, as a pack.

200.description: The records, in the order asked, each followed by its description or payload if the repository has it, as a pack: each object a 32-byte id, a little-endian u64 length and the object's encoding. At most 64 MiB, but for a record alone

origin-more.description: Present if the pack stopped short: ask again for the records after the last it holds

400.description: An object is a blob or a tree, which only leave by walking a snapshot

404.description: The repository or a record does not exist

post.summary:
Fetches the objects of a snapshot the caller lacks, as a pack: the only
way trees and blobs leave a repository.

200.description: The trees and blobs, parents before children, as a pack, of at most 64 MiB, but for an object alone

origin-more.description: Present if the pack stopped short: ask again, skipping the objects it holds

404.description: The repository or the snapshot does not exist

get.summary:
Lists the statements about a record, in the order the repository
received them.
Lists the targets, with their tips, authorities and requirements.

post.summary: Creates a target at the tip of another, ordered by this server.

404.description: The repository or the target to start from does not exist

409.description: The name is taken, or this server wouldn't order the target

post.summary:
Issues a token acting for the caller, with a scope narrowing their
rights, signed by the server, which verifies it without storing it.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: The repository whose policy the scope is checked against

403.description: The caller isn't signed in, or the scope reaches beyond their rights

get.summary:
Lists a directory of a snapshot: a target's tip, or a revision's or an
acceptance's. Withheld entries keep their place.

parameters.name: at
parameters.description:
The snapshot: a target, such as `main`, or `revision:<id>` or
`acceptance:<id>`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The directory or file: the root by default.

400.description: The path is a file, or the record has no snapshot

403.description: The caller reads nothing under the path

404.description: The repository, the target, the record or the path does not exist

get.summary: Tells the caller who they are and what they may do in the repository.

401.description: The token is invalid or expired

Acceptance.description:
One landing on a target, signed by the target's authority.

Acceptances form a hash chain per target: each names the one before it,
and its sequence number is its position in the target's log.

In JSON, the body's fields and the signature, in hex.

evidence.description: The statements the policy relied on.

oneOf.description:
The acceptance of the `policy` target in force when this one landed.
Absent only for the first acceptance of `policy`, which nothing
precedes.
The acceptance before this one, absent only for the first.

seq.description: The position in the target's log, from 0.

state.description: The target's snapshot after this landing.

Annotation.description: A statement, and whether its issuer superseded it.

oneOf.description: The first statement from the same issuer that supersedes it.

ApiError.description: What went wrong with a request.

oneOf.description: The state of a target after one of its acceptances.

acceptance.description: The state of a target after one of its acceptances.

oneOf.description: Another revision, such as the one below in a stack.

revision.description: Another revision, such as the one below in a stack.

Base.description: What a revision was made on top of.

oneOf.description: The target requires these statements about the subject.

evidence.description: The target requires these statements about the subject.

oneOf.description:
Both sides changed these paths. The `core.conflict` statement lists
them too.

conflict.description:
Both sides changed these paths. The `core.conflict` statement lists
them too.

cursor.description:
The sequence number of the op log entry it comes from. Reading from
it delivers the events of the entries after it.

Event.description: Something that happened, and where it is in the op log.

oneOf.description: A statement was issued.
Its verdict.
A revision was created.
A target advanced.

seq.description: The acceptance's position in its log.

oneOf.description: A landing waits for a statement it requires.

subject.description: What the statement must be about.

EventKind.description:
What happened. In JSON, the `event` field names it, as
[`EventKind::name`] does.

FetchRecords.description:
Asks for records by id: revisions, statements and acceptances. Each
comes with the attachment it carries, if the repository has it: a
revision's description, a statement's payload. Snapshots are fetched
with [`FetchSnapshot`] instead.

ids.description:
The records, returned in this order, each followed by its
attachment. Those the caller may not read are left out. A response
that stops short, with the [`MORE`] header, holds those up to the
last record it has: ask again for those after it.

FetchSnapshot.description:
Asks for the objects of a snapshot that the caller lacks: its trees and
blobs, walked from its root. This is the only way blobs and trees leave
a repository, so what each caller may read is checked by path: the
content of paths they may not read is withheld, though it keeps its
place in the trees.

have.description:
Snapshots the caller holds whole. Whatever one of them holds at the
same path is skipped, so only what changed since comes. Those the
repository doesn't have are ignored.

of.description:
The record whose snapshot it is: a revision or an acceptance. Only a
record's snapshot is walked, never a tree within one, whose paths
would be read as others.

paths.description:
Only these files and directories, with everything under them, and
the trees on the way to them. Everything by default.

skip.description:
Skip this many of the objects, which earlier parts brought: a
response that stops short has the [`MORE`] header.

Head.description: The latest acceptance of a target.

seq.description: Its position in the log, from 0.

Inputs.description:
What a statement depended on.

The input digest of a snapshot hashes the ids it stores at `paths`, with
`definition` and `toolchain`. A statement that declares inputs and isn't
`external` is promoted to every revision with the same input digest.

external.description:
Whether the claim also depended on things outside the snapshot, such
as the network, which makes it never promotable.

paths.description: The files and directories read, each covering everything under it.

toolchain.description: The tools that ran it, such as the hash of `rustc -V`.

Inventory.description:
What a repository holds of a change: its records, by id, to compare
with another node's.

heads.description: Those no other revision of the change evolves from.

revisions.description:
Its revisions, in the order the repository received them: none if it
has never heard of the change.

statements.description:
The statements about its revisions, and about those statements, in
no particular order.

InventoryRequest.description: Asks what a repository holds of some changes.

expires.description: When it expires, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

token.description: The token, to send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

LandRequest.description: Asks the queue to land something.

oneOf.description:
The target to land on. For a change, the target its stack is on by
default; a target needs one.
It landed.

source.description: The revision or acceptance the acceptance names.

oneOf.description: The target already has it, so nothing landed.

unchanged.description: The target already has it, so nothing landed.

oneOf.description: It waits, and the queue keeps it.

pending.description: It waits, and the queue keeps it.

landings.description:
How each landing went: one for each change of a stack that the
target didn't have, from the bottom, up to the first that waits.

Level.description: What a caller may do with a path.

kind.description: A file, an executable, a symlink or a directory.

withheld.description:
Whether its content is withheld from the caller: it keeps its
place, but can't be read.

LogEntry.description: One acceptance of a target's log.

acceptance.description: The acceptance, whose `seq` is its position in the log.

from.description: The target whose tip it starts at.

Page.description: A batch of events, and the cursor to read the next batch from.

generation.description:
The generation of the op log the cursor is of: pass it with the
cursor, which means nothing in another.

next.description: The cursor after the entries read: pass it to the next read.

PathAccess.description:
What a caller may do with every path: the level of the most specific
path it lists at or above it. The root is always listed.

Pending.description: A landing that waits, kept in the queue to be listed and retried.

expires.description:
When the token of its submitter, whom it's retried for, expires, in
seconds since the Unix epoch, if it's a scoped one. Once it has, the
landing is no longer retried: it waits until it's landed again.

subject.description:
What the evidence must be about: the revision that would land, or
the merged snapshot of a target. A conflict is about the revision,
or the acceptance, that didn't merge.

PromoteRequest.description: Asks for the results of other records to be promoted to one.

subject.description:
The record: a revision, an acceptance, or a waiting landing's
snapshot.

oneOf.description: A change, as of its head.

change.description: A change, as of its head.

oneOf.description: Another target, as of its tip.

target.description: Another target, as of its tip.

RepoName.description:
The name of a repository on a server: ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_`
and `-`, not starting with `.`.

RepoSummary.description: A repository, as listed by the server.

Requirement.description:
A statement that landing needs: of `kind`, with `verdict`, from one of
`issuer`, about what lands.

Revision.description:
One immutable version of a change.

Editing, rebasing or handing a change to someone else creates a new
revision of the same change, whose predecessors are the revisions it
evolves from.

base.description: What the revision was made on top of.

change.description: The change this is a version of.

deps.description:
The exact revisions this one requires: the changes below it in a
stack.

description.description: The intent, written for humans and agents.

predecessors.description:
The revisions this one evolves from. Two make it a convergence of
divergent heads.

snapshot.description: The root tree of the files.

heads.description:
Those that no other revision of the change evolves from: more than
one is divergence.

revisions.description: Every revision, in the order the repository received them.

Rights.description:
What a caller may do, resolved from the policy in force and narrowed by
their token's scope.

annotate.description: The kinds of statements they may issue.

groups.description: The policy's groups the caller is a member of.

land.description: The targets they may land on, but `policy`.

paths.description: What they may do with each path.

oneOf.description:
Who the caller is: `None` for an anonymous caller, or the node's own
user.

scope.description: The token's scope, if the caller came with a scoped token.

oneOf.description: A revision of a change.
Another target, as of one of its acceptances.

target.description: Another target, as of one of its acceptances.

Statement.description:
An attributable claim about another record: a check result, a review, a
conflict, an abandonment.

Statements are permanent. An issuer revises one by issuing another that
supersedes it. A promoted statement carries another one over to a record
with the same input digest, pointing at it instead of copying its issuer.

oneOf.description:
What the claim depended on, which lets it be promoted to revisions
with the same inputs.

kind.description: What kind of claim it is.

oneOf.description: Free-form details, defined by whoever owns the kind.

The statement this one promotes: its kind, verdict, inputs and
payload hold here too, because the input digests are equal. The
issuer is whoever promoted it, the original's stays on the original.

subject.description: The record the claim is about.

oneOf.description: A statement from the same issuer that this one replaces.
The outcome, the only field core interprets.

Stored.description: What putting a batch of records did.

new.description: How many of the objects the repository didn't have yet.

TargetInfo.description: A target, where it is, and who orders it under the policy in force.

oneOf.description: The node that orders it, if the policy names one.

requirements.description: The statements landing on it needs.

TokenRequest.description:
Asks a server for a token with a narrower scope, for an agent or a CI
runner.

scope.description: What it may do: a part of what the caller may do.

ttl.description: How long it lasts, such as `1h`.
